kind: mid-work, supersedes CP2's open CI blocker
summary: The CI dispatch anomaly from CP2 is resolved and both PRs are merged on real, current-base CI success. Root cause found and fixed per the operator's own diagnostic sequence, not worked around.

rootCause.diagnosis: NOT a paths/paths-ignore filter (ci.yml carries none; confirmed identical to origin/main's copy) and NOT Actions being disabled or a stale required-check name (both checked and ruled out). The actual cause: after PR #443 squash-merged, this branch's own commit history still had the PRE-squash commit (1f04459) as its base rather than the post-squash main commit (5e43fc0) -- a classic squash-then-continue-on-the-same-branch divergence. GitHub's PR mergeable state silently went CONFLICTING/DIRTY, and while in that state no pull_request-triggered check-suite was being created at all (a push and a close/reopen both failed to trigger one). A manually workflow_dispatch-triggered run DID succeed (proving the code and CI environment were fine), which was the key diagnostic separating a webhook/event problem from a runner/YAML/quota problem.
rootCause.fix: git rebase origin/main on the engine branch (git recognized 1f04459 as already-applied via patch-id and skipped it automatically, replaying only the two genuinely new commits with zero conflicts), then force-push. This simultaneously fixed the phantom merge conflict (mergeable flipped to MERGEABLE) and unblocked pull_request check-suite creation (a real run started automatically on the force-push).
rootCause.credit: Diagnosed by the operator's own directed sequence (check paths filter -> Actions enabled -> workflow YAML valid -> branch protection -> and the workflow_dispatch escalation as both an unblock and a diagnostic), not found independently.
